statements.text: A document MUST be a JSON object.
A document MUST NOT contain a top-level member that the table above does not list.
A document that targets this draft MUST declare "floorspec": "0.3".
A reader MUST reject a document that declares a version the reader does not implement, with the diagnostic FS-DOC-001.

A reader that implements this draft MUST also read a document that declares "0.1" or "0.2": it MUST apply the schema of the draft the document declares to it at the schema tier, and otherwise read it as a 0.3 document in which every member that a later draft than the one it declares adds is absent.
Every level MUST reference a building.
Every junction, wall, separator, room and slab MUST reference a level.
An element MUST NOT contain a member that its kind's table in this specification does not list.

Every object this specification defines that is not an element — the project, the site and its location, a wall's base and top, a junction's join, a layer, a texture — MUST NOT contain a member that its table does not list. The content of extras and of extension data is not restricted.
Every member MUST have the type, and lie in the range, that its table and its section give.
Every element MAY carry these members, in addition to those of its kind:
A reader MUST treat an absent member exactly as if it were present with its default value.
A writer MAY omit a member whose value equals its constant default.
Every extension name MUST match the pattern ^(FS|EXT|[A-Z0-9]{2,8})_[A-Za-z0-9]+$.
Every version in extensionsUsed MUST match ^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$.
extensionsRequired MUST NOT name an extension twice.
Every name in extensionsRequired MUST also be a member of extensionsUsed.
Every member name of an extensions object, at the top level or on an element, MUST be a member of extensionsUsed.
A reader MUST reject a document whose extensionsRequired names an extension the reader does not implement, with the diagnostic FS-DOC-002.

A reader MUST accept a document that uses optional extensions it does not implement, and MUST NOT let their data affect anything it derives, except the core members of their extension elements — fallback, host and clearances (12.5) — from which it derives exactly what chapters 12 and 13 define, and nothing else.
A writer MUST preserve the data of every extension it does not implement, unchanged.
A deriver MUST NOT let extras affect any derived value.
A writer MUST preserve extras it does not itself manage, unchanged.
trueNorth MUST be greater than −180,000,000 and at most 180,000,000.
A level's height MUST be greater than zero.
A level's floorThickness and ceilingHeight, when present, MUST be greater than zero.
A length MUST be a JSON integer — no fraction and no exponent — with an absolute value of at most 9,007,199,254,740,991 (2⁵³ − 1).
A deriver MUST compute each derived coordinate as an exact value and round it once, with round() (nearest integer, ties to even), to produce the derived output.
A deriver MUST interpret plan coordinates in this system, so that, seen from above, a rotation from +X towards +Y is counter-clockwise.
An angle MUST be a JSON integer.
A polygon in a document MUST be simple — its edges meet only at consecutive shared vertices, no two vertices coincide — and MUST enclose a positive area.
An element ID MUST match the pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$.
An element ID MUST be unique across all of a document's collections, not only within its own.
A program item's ID and an extension element's ID MUST match the pattern of 3.1.1, and MUST be unique among all the IDs of the document, as element IDs are.
A reference MUST be a string that matches the ID pattern of 3.1.
Every reference MUST resolve to an element of the collection that its member names in this table.
Every reference to a type MUST resolve to a type of the kind its member names in this table.
A wall's or separator's start and end junctions MUST be on the wall's or separator's own level.
A level named by a wall's base.level or top.level MUST be in the same building as the wall's own level.
A room's function MUST be either one of the terms in this table or an extension term (4.2).
The extension named in an extension term MUST be a member of extensionsUsed.
A layer's function MUST be one of the terms in this table.
Two junctions on the same level MUST NOT have the same position.
An edge's start and end MUST be different junctions.
Two edges MUST NOT connect the same pair of junctions, in either order.
Two edges on the same level MUST NOT cross: their location lines MUST NOT meet in a single point that lies in the interior of both.
A junction MUST NOT lie in the interior of the location line of an edge on its level.
The location lines of two edges on the same level MUST NOT overlap in a segment of positive length.
A wall MUST have effective layers.
A wall justified "coreFace" MUST have at least one core layer, and its core layers MUST be consecutive.
A deriver MUST compute every corner sequence as defined in this section.
A deriver MUST derive each wall's four face ends as defined in this section and 5.8, rounded as 2.2 requires.
A wall's outline MUST be a simple polygon with positive area and counter-clockwise orientation.
A deriver MUST derive the junction fill of every junction with three or more edges and the default join.

A junction fill with fewer than three vertices, or whose shoelace area is zero, is empty. A junction fill that is not empty MUST be a simple polygon with positive area and counter-clockwise orientation.
A join MUST have exactly one of the three forms in this table: kind "mitre" and no other member, or kind "butt" and a through array of one or two wall IDs.
Every wall named in through MUST be one of the junction's edges.
With one wall in through, the junction MUST have exactly two edges, and they MUST NOT be collinear.

With two walls in through, the two MUST leave the junction in exactly opposite directions with coincident face lines — the left face line of each is the right face line of the other — and at most one other edge MAY lie on each side of the line they form.
A deriver MUST apply a junction's butt join as defined in this section.
top MUST have either level or height, and MUST NOT have both; offset MUST NOT appear with height.
A wall's top elevation MUST be greater than its base elevation.
A deriver MUST derive each wall's base and top elevations as defined in this section.
These conditions make a document worse, not invalid. A validator SHOULD report them with the codes of chapter 10.
A deriver MUST derive the room polygon of every bounded face as defined in this section.
A room's anchor MUST lie in a bounded face of its level: not in the unbounded face, and not on any location line.
Two rooms MUST NOT have their anchors in the same face.
The room polygon of a room's face MUST NOT be degenerate.
A room's anchor MUST lie strictly inside the room polygon of its face: inside the outer ring, and outside and off every hole ring.
A deriver MUST compute each room's net area exactly, from the rounded vertices of its room polygon.
A validator SHOULD report these with the codes of chapter 10.
A slab's thickness MUST be greater than zero.
A slab's purpose, when present, MUST be a slab purpose of this table.
offset MUST NOT be negative.
width and height MUST be greater than zero, and sill MUST NOT be negative.
An opening's clearOpening MUST NOT have an area unless the opening's fill is a window type.
Every opening MUST resolve an effective width and an effective height.
An opening's effective clearOpening, when it has one, MUST NOT be wider than the opening's effective width nor taller than its effective height.
An opening MUST lie within its wall's length: offset + width MUST NOT exceed the length of the wall's location line.
An opening MUST lie within its wall's height: sill + height MUST NOT exceed the wall's top elevation minus its base elevation.
Two openings on the same wall MUST NOT overlap: if their intervals along the wall overlap by a positive length, their vertical intervals MUST NOT also overlap by a positive length.
A deriver MUST derive each opening's start point, end point, sill elevation and head elevation as defined in this section, rounded as 2.2 requires.

A deriver MUST derive the clear opening of each opening that has an effective clearOpening, with exactly the members declared, and MUST NOT derive one for any other opening or derive an area that is not declared.
A validator SHOULD report this with the code of chapter 10.
A type MUST have a kind from this table.
Every type MAY also carry name, extensions and extras (1.4).

A type's or a material's source MUST have exactly the members of this table, each always present: a library that is an absolute https URI with an authority, a version that matches the pattern of 1.6.7, and an item that matches the pattern of 3.1.1.
A reader MUST resolve a typed property to the element's own member if present, otherwise to its type's member if present, otherwise to the property's default if it has one.
A layers array MUST contain at least one layer, and every layer's thickness MUST be greater than zero.
A door or window type's width and height, when present, MUST be greater than zero, and its sill MUST NOT be negative.
A door type's operation, when present, MUST be a door operation of this section, and a window type's a window operation.
A clear opening's width and height MUST be greater than zero, its area, when present, MUST be an integer from 1 to 2⁵³ − 1, and a door type's clear opening MUST NOT have an area.
A clear opening's area MUST NOT exceed the product of its width and its height.
A door or window type's clear opening MUST NOT be wider than the type's width, when the type has one, nor taller than its height, when it has one.
A material's color MUST match ^#[0-9a-f]{6}$.
A texture's size MUST be two lengths greater than zero.
An asset MUST have exactly one of path and uri.
A path MUST be relative, use / as its separator, contain no empty, . or .. segment, and have no : in its first segment.
A validator SHOULD report these with the codes of chapter 10.
A document MUST be a well-formed JSON text in UTF-8, without a byte order mark.
An object in a document MUST NOT contain the same member name twice.
A string in a document MUST NOT contain an unpaired surrogate, whether literally or as a \u escape.
A canonicalizer MUST produce exactly the canonical form of every valid document it is given.
Canonicalization MUST NOT change what a document means: the canonical form of a document has the same derived values as the document.
A deriver MUST compute a document's content hash as this section defines it.
A validator MUST report a document as valid if, and only if, it reports no diagnostic with severity error.
A validator MUST report each condition the catalogue lists as a diagnostic with the catalogued code, severity and elements.
A validator MUST NOT report a diagnostic that this section says is not evaluated.
A fix is advice. A validator MAY offer a fix for any diagnostic, and an editor applies a fix only when a person or an agent chooses to.
A program, a program item and an adjacency MUST have only the members of their tables, each of the type and in the range its table gives.
A program item's function MUST be a room function as 4.1.1 allows, and an extension term in it MUST name an extension that is a member of extensionsUsed, as 4.2.1 requires of a room's.
An adjacency MUST NOT relate an item to itself: a and b MUST be different items.
Two adjacencies MUST NOT have the same pair and the same kind.
A pair that has a "forbidden" adjacency MUST NOT also have a "required" or a "preferred" one.
A deriver MUST derive these values for every program item of a valid document, comparing areas exactly.
A deriver MUST derive these values for every adjacency of a valid document.
A validator SHOULD report these with the codes of chapter 10.
A validator MUST NOT report an unmet program — a count, an area or an adjacency — with severity error.
Every value in extensionsUsed MUST be a version string or a declaration object, and a declaration object MUST have a version and no member but version and schema.
A declaration's schema MUST be an absolute https URI with an authority, as an asset's uri is (8.6).
A reader MUST treat a declaration object exactly as the version string of its version member: the schema member never changes what a document means.
A reader MAY use a declaration's schema to validate the extension's data.

Known extensions MUST be a set of registry entries each matching the registry entry schema, no two with the same name and version, in which the relation "an entry of X requires Y" between extension names has no cycle.
A validator configured with known extensions that break 12.2.1 MUST report the diagnostic FS-CFG-001, and no other diagnostic, for every document.
A validator MUST evaluate a version range exactly as this section defines.
A document that uses X at a version at which X is known MUST also use every extension that X's entry requires.
Each extension it requires MUST be used at a version that satisfies the range X's entry gives for it.
Every collection in X's top-level extension data (12.5) MUST be named in the kinds of X's entry.
Every element in a collection of X MUST have the fallback parts that its kind in X's entry requires: an asset when the kind's fallback.asset is true, and a symbol when its fallback.symbol is true.
Every extension term of X (4.2) in a room's or a program item's function MUST be listed in the roomFunctions of X's entry.
Top-level extension data that has a collections member MUST have, as its value, an object whose member names are collection names and whose members are objects mapping IDs to extension elements.
Every extension element MUST have a fallback, and its core members MUST have the types their tables give.
A fallback's asset MUST be an asset whose mediaType is model/gltf-binary or model/gltf+json, and its symbol an asset whose mediaType is image/svg+xml or image/png.
A deriver MUST derive the fallback of every extension element of a valid document as this section and 13.2 define.
Software that draws a fallback's model SHOULD place it in the element's frame exactly by this mapping.
Software that draws a fallback's symbol in plan SHOULD draw it on the footprint of the element's box exactly as this table defines.
A deriver MUST compute facing vectors, directions and frames exactly as this section defines.
A box MUST have exactly the members min and max, each an array of three lengths.
Each of a box's three extents, max minus min on one axis, MUST be at least 1,280 base units (1 mm).
A host MUST have exactly the members of one of the three forms, each of the type its table gives: offset and height MUST NOT be negative, and rotation MUST lie in (−180,000,000, 180,000,000].
A wallFace host's offset MUST NOT exceed the length of its wall's location line.
A wallFace host's height MUST NOT exceed its wall's top elevation minus its base elevation.
A surface host's position MUST lie strictly inside the room polygon of its room's face: inside the outer ring, and outside and off every hole ring (6.3.4).
An extension element's fallback.level MUST be its host's level: the wall's level for a wallFace host, the room's level for a surface host, and the host's level for a free host.
A deriver MUST derive the placement of every extension element that has a host, in a valid document.

A clearances object MUST map names matching ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ to envelopes that have exactly the members of the table, each of the type the table gives, and MUST appear only on door types, window types and extension elements.
A deriver MUST derive every clearance envelope of a valid document as this section defines.
A deriver MUST derive every pair of envelopes of different owners that overlap, as this section defines.
A deriver MUST link two rooms in the door graph exactly when this section says they are linked.
A deriver MUST derive these values for every room of a valid document.
A validator SHOULD report these with the codes of chapter 10.
A validator MUST NOT report FS-LINT-012, FS-LINT-013 or FS-LINT-014 for a building that is not evaluated, and MUST NOT report FS-LINT-012 or FS-LINT-013 for a room of a building that has no entry.
A validator MUST NOT report a circulation condition — a building with no entry, an unreachable room or a sleeping room reached through another — with severity error.
A room's floor MUST have only the members of this table, each of the type the table gives, and its thickness MUST be greater than zero.
A deriver MUST derive the floor of every room — its top, bottom and box — as this section defines them.

A room's ceiling MUST have exactly the members of one of the three forms, each of the type its table gives: height, border and depth MUST be greater than zero, a ridge MUST be an array of exactly two points, a pitch's rise and run MUST be integers from 1 to 2⁵³ − 1, and slopes MUST be "both", "left" or "right".
A room's ceiling MUST be above its floor: the least exact elevation of its ceiling over its room polygon MUST be greater than the top of its floor.
A vaulted ceiling's two ridge points MUST NOT be the same point.
A deriver MUST compute the elevation of a vaulted ceiling, and its low and high over its room polygon, exactly as this section defines them, rounding each value it outputs once.

A tray ceiling's border MUST fit its room: for every edge of every ring, the edge from the rounded Vᵢ' to the rounded Vᵢ₊₁' MUST run the way the edge from Vᵢ to Vᵢ₊₁ runs — the dot product of the two is greater than zero — and the rounded moved rings, taken as a room polygon, MUST NOT be degenerate (6.2).
A deriver MUST derive the centre of every tray ceiling as this section defines it.
A deriver MUST derive every room's ceiling as this section defines it.
A deriver MUST derive the frame of every surface host at the elevation this section gives it.
A deriver MUST derive the outline, top, bottom and box of every slab as this section defines them.

A roof MUST have only the members of these tables, each of the type the tables give: its pitch and every edge's pitch MUST have a rise and a run that are integers from 1 to 2⁵³ − 1; its overhang and every edge's overhang MUST NOT be negative; its thickness MUST be greater than zero; every member name of edges MUST be an edge index written in decimal without leading zeros; and an edge whose gable is true MUST NOT have a pitch.
Every member name of a roof's edges MUST name an edge of its footprint: it is less than the number of the footprint's vertices.
A roof's edges MUST be all level or none of them level.
A roof that is not flat MUST have at least one sloped edge.
Two consecutive edges of a roof's footprint MUST NOT be collinear.

A roof's eave outline MUST fit its footprint: for every edge, the edge from the rounded Vᵢ' to the rounded Vᵢ₊₁' MUST run the way the edge from Vᵢ to Vᵢ₊₁ runs — the dot product of the two is greater than zero — and the eave outline MUST be a simple polygon (2.6) that runs the way the footprint runs.

A deriver MUST derive the surface of every flat roof, of every shed roof that 16.4.2 says is derived, and of every equal-pitch roof that 16.4.3 says is derived, exactly as this section defines it, and MUST derive no surface for any other roof; a validator MUST report every other roof with FS-LINT-015.
A deriver MUST derive every roof as this section defines it.

A stair MUST have exactly the members of its table, each of the type its table gives: width, tread and maxRiser MUST be greater than zero, risers MUST be an integer from 1 to 2⁵³ − 1, rotation MUST lie in (−180,000,000, 180,000,000], a handrail's height MUST be greater than zero, and a stair MUST have exactly one of risers and maxRiser.
A stair's to MUST be a level of the building its level is in, and MUST NOT be its level.

A stair's form MUST have exactly the members of one of the five forms, each of the type its table gives: risersBeforeTurn and winders MUST be integers from 1 to 2⁵³ − 1, gap MUST NOT be negative, diameter MUST be greater than zero, sweep MUST be an integer from 1 to 2⁵³ − 1, and a quarter-turn winder stair MUST NOT have a gap.
A spiral stair's width MUST NOT be more than half its diameter.
A stair's rise MUST be greater than zero.

A stair's riser count MUST fit its form: at least 2 for a straight or a spiral stair; for an L-shaped or a U-shaped stair, risersBeforeTurn at least 2 and the riser count at least risersBeforeTurn + 2, so that each flight has a tread; and for a winder stair, at least risersBeforeTurn + winders.
A deriver MUST derive these values for every stair of a valid document, as this section and 17.3 define them.
A deriver MUST derive the steps, the run and the walkline of every straight, L-shaped and U-shaped stair of a valid document as this section defines them.

A deriver MUST derive the headroom of every straight, L-shaped and U-shaped stair of a valid document that has one, as headroom, exactly as this section defines it, and no headroom member for one that has none.
A deriver MUST NOT derive steps, run, walkline or headroom for a winder or a spiral stair.
A validator SHOULD report FS-LINT-016 (info) for each winder and each spiral stair.
A material's metallic and roughness, when present, MUST be integers from 0 to 1000.

A texture MUST have at least one map, and MUST have exactly the members of its table, each of the type its table gives: size two lengths greater than zero (8.5.2), offset a point, and rotation an angle in (−180,000,000, 180,000,000].
Every map MUST be an asset whose mediaType is image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp or image/ktx2.
Software that draws a material's maps on a surface this section lists SHOULD place them exactly as this section defines.
An asset's byteLength, when present, MUST be an integer from 0 to 2⁵³ − 1.
A package validator MUST report FS-INV-1005 for each asset located by path for which the package has no file at that path.
A package validator MUST report FS-INV-1006 for each asset whose file's SHA-256 digest is not its sha256, and FS-INV-1007 for each asset with a byteLength that is not its file's length in bytes.
A validator that is not given the files of the package MUST NOT report FS-INV-1005, FS-INV-1006 or FS-INV-1007.
A wall's finishes, its face finishes and their regions MUST have exactly the members of their tables, each of the type its table gives: a region's from, to, bottom and top MUST NOT be negative.
A region's to MUST be greater than its from, and its top greater than its bottom.
A region MUST NOT extend beyond its wall: its to MUST NOT exceed the length of the wall's location line, and its top MUST NOT exceed the wall's top elevation minus its base elevation.
Two regions of one face MUST NOT overlap: no point may lie strictly inside both.

A deriver MUST derive the finishes of every valid document: for each room, its floor's and its ceiling's finish, when it has one; and for each side of each wall whose finish resolves to a material or that has regions, the room it faces, if any, the material that finishes the rest of the face, if any, where that material comes from, and the face's regions.
An option set and an option MUST have exactly the members of their tables, each of the type its table gives.
An option set's primary MUST be one of the set's own options.
An element of any other collection — a building, a level, a type, a material, an asset, an option set or an option — and a program item MUST NOT have an option member.
What this specification says a validator reports for a design, a deriver derives for it or an exporter writes for it MUST be exactly what it says of the design's view, as a document.
A reference (3.2) MUST NOT resolve to an element that is in an option, unless the referring element is in that same option.

A validator MUST evaluate every invariant other than the reference and option invariants for the view of every checked design, as 10.3 orders them, and so MUST report a document invalid when the view of any checked design has an error.

A validator MUST report every diagnostic of the primary design's view as it is, and every other diagnostic of an option design's view with the member design, the ID of that option: a diagnostic of an option design's view that matches one of the primary design's view — the same code, severity and elements, each of the primary design's matched at most once — MUST NOT be reported again.
A deriver MUST derive for a valid document exactly the values chapters 5 to 7 and 11 to 18 define for the view of the design its design input gives, or of the primary design when it has none.
A deriver MUST NOT derive any value for a design input that names an option set the document does not have or maps a set to an option that is not that set's, nor for a design whose view is not valid.
A deriver MUST derive options as this section defines it for every valid document that has an option set, and MUST NOT derive an options member for one that has none.
An exporter SHOULD export the primary design unless it is asked for another, and SHOULD record which design it exported.
A validator SHOULD report FS-LINT-017 (info) for each option set with exactly one option: it has nothing to choose between.
